title: Review: the Part 3 item definition, both safety concepts, the SYS.1 elicitation set, the SYS.2 system requirements and the four validation measures

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Automated review pass authored in the same session as the records it covers. It is NOT an independent review: the reviewing role is the authoring role and the runtime is the same one that wrote the artifacts. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 that makes it an automated review and nothing more.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Provenance repair by a separate session (opencode-2026-10-01-provenance-repair), not a re-review. All 10 reviewed_ids digests in this record were re-derived from the artefact files as they stand on disk in the correct profile (synthetic_reference).  10 of 10 named artefacts have been revised or had their bytes replaced since this review was issued, so this record is re-issued at revision 2 and its digest for those artefacts now names the current revision; per-artefact detail, including the superseded digest and the basis for each classification, is in digest_corrections.  The findings, dispositions, scope, checklist and reviewer_identity of the original pass are untouched by this repair. The digest refresh does not carry the weight of a re-review: the original reviewer session did not examine the current revision of the revised artefacts, and no substantive re-examination was performed here.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session. The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime; no platform-issued session id was available, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. The reviewing role is the same role that authored the records, so this pass has NO independence from the work it reviews and must not be read as confirmation. It is recorded as coverage of the review obligation, not as discharge of it.

scope: Every record in ids_a at revision 1, plus the pre-existing records they were written from: FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001, FB2-SAF-SGO-000001, FB2-SAF-FSR-000001..000004, FB2-HW-TSR-000001..000004, FB2-SW-SWR-000001..000003 and FB2-SAF-ANL-000001..000004. Findings were raised against the pre-existing records and no pre-existing record was edited.

findings.description: The safety goal's timing budget does not close: 85 ms of serial work plus a 20 ms margin against a 100 ms interval.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic over FB2-SAF-SGO-000001's own timing_budget.allocation and fault_tolerant_time_interval_ms. Performed by hand, not by the validator, whose FTTI rule does not fire because it looks the interval up under a field name this record does not use.

findings.description: The contactor reaction requirement's 30 ms acceptance threshold contradicts its own 35 ms rationale and the safety goal's 40 ms allocation for the same chain.
findings.evidence: Three figures read side by side: FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 acceptance_criteria[0] threshold 30, its rationale '30 ms mechanical opening + 5 ms feedback = 35 ms', and FB2-SAF-SGO-000001's contactor_command 5 + contactor_mechanical 30 + feedback_verification 5.

findings.description: The independent monitor's justification cites a 115 ms main-path figure that appears in no record.
findings.evidence: A corpus-wide search for the literal 115 returns only this rationale and the identical text in FB2-HW-TSR-000004. The nearest real figure is the safety goal's 85 ms serial sum.

findings.description: FB2-HW-TSR-000004 and FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 are the same sentence at two ISO 26262 levels, and their shared monitoring-coverage criterion is a disjunction with an undefined term.
findings.evidence: Byte comparison of the two records' statement, rationale, safety_allocation and acceptance_criteria fields: identical in all four.

findings.description: The system requirement requires a degraded-to-fault boundary to be declared but does not supply a value for it, so it is satisfiable and not yet satisfied.
findings.evidence: The acceptance criterion 'Degraded-to-fault boundary declared, Numerical value or named rule separating degraded from fault, 1, declared value' has no corresponding value anywhere in the corpus. The record states this in its own open_point field rather than leaving a reader to discover it.

dispositions.action: Not resolved by editing the baselined safety goal. Recorded as a finding; the technical safety concept allocates a closing budget and names the departure; an arithmetic check added to the review checklist as FB2-PIM-IMP-000001; the correction referred to change control as INST-004. Registered as risk RSK-001.

Not resolved. The choice between restating the threshold and reducing the reaction is an engineering decision with a safety consequence. The technical safety concept budgets the chain at 35 ms and names the conflict. Referred as INST-004.
Not resolved. The technical safety concept restates the justification on the 85 ms figure that exists and uses no unsourced number. Referred as INST-004.
Not resolved. FB2-SYS-SYR-000005 was authored at system level to give the decomposition somewhere to land, but the two identical records remain. Referred as INST-004 and registered as risk RSK-006.

The requirement deliberately does not invent the value. It is recorded as an open point on the requirement itself, so the gap is visible at the requirement rather than in a finding that a reader might not connect to it.

limitations: Automated review only. It is not independent confirmation, not a functional-safety expert review and not a human approval. The reviewing role authored four of the records it reviews.

The concept records were checked for internal consistency and for consistency with the pre-existing records they name. They were NOT checked against the standard: no clause text was consulted, so the standards_mappings on every new record assert the conceptual role of each clause and nothing about its wording.

The numeric checks were performed by hand on the fields of the records named. The validator's automated FTTI rule does not fire on FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 and that gap is itself reported as finding FB2-REV-FND-000025 rather than closed by adjusting a record.

No coverage claim was verified. Every diagnostic-coverage figure in the technical concept is either a requirement-side claim, an analytical estimate on an assumed noise distribution, or an assumption, and the review confirmed that each is labelled as such rather than that any is true.
The four validation measures and their four blocked executions were reviewed for planning quality only. None has been executed and the review does not claim otherwise.
